issues.competing_evidence: HST/FGS solutions span 6.02±0.46 mas (Harrison+99), 6.06±0.44 (Harrison+04), 8.30±0.41 (Nelan & Bond 2013), and 7.3±0.2 mas in the Harrison & McArthur 2016 AAS abstract; Harrison+16 footnote gives 7.41±0.20 mas. Gaia EDR3 geometric posterior is 112.35 pc and VLBI is 114±2 pc.
issues.why_it_matters: Distance changes luminosities and distance-dependent accretion/WD-atmosphere interpretations; the HST re-reductions are not mutually consistent.
issues.needed_action: Keep every astrometric solution separate and use Gaia geometric posterior only for the compatibility distance. If one historical solution is needed, retrieve/compare the 2016 HST/FGS reduction products or obtain clarification from its authors; do not average.

issues.competing_evidence: Sion+10 gives 46 kK at E(B−V)=0.04 and 55 kK at 0.07 with 166 pc; Sion & Godon+15 refits at 114–120 pc and gives 45–50 kK, representative 47 kK, with fixed assumed 0.95 Msun.
issues.why_it_matters: WD heating/accretion comparisons depend on reddening, distance, mass and fit assumptions; averaging would hide model branches.
issues.needed_action: For a future canonical summary, decide whether to display the updated-distance refit as the preferred model branch while retaining older reddening branches, or show all branches without a single preferred range. No new atmosphere refit is performed here.

issues.competing_evidence: Accretion-state-dependent DNOs vary 7.81→6.59→2.91→2.85 s in 1996 (Mauche & Robinson 2001); XRISM line width implies 16–44 s only if rotational, while no 10–50 s timing signal was detected (Ishida+26); Sharp+26 reports optical QPO-like peaks 0.25–8 h.
issues.why_it_matters: Conflating these clocks would produce a false WD spin distribution and could bias comparisons with WD pulsars or LPTs.
issues.needed_action: Keep numeric wd_spin_period_s blank. Decide later whether a distinct model-inferred spin-candidate field should expose 16–44 s; keep DNOs and optical QPOs in their own component-qualified fields unless independent coherent spin periodicity is detected.

issues.competing_evidence: Ridder+23 Table 4 gives 9.0±0.9×10−10 and 4.1(+0.5/−0.4)×10−11 erg cm−2 s−1 in nominal unabsorbed 1–10 keV, based on Swift spectra; the two points are maxima in different bands and their SS Cyg observation IDs/model/NH/conversion are not printed.
issues.why_it_matters: Flux comparison and luminosity interpretation depend on band conversion, absorption convention and epoch; values are not proven simultaneous with radio.
issues.needed_action: If exact Swift extraction must be reproduced, identify ObsIDs and fitted model/NH or PIMMS settings in the UK Swift archive/Ridder materials. Retain both published estimates with this limitation until then.

issues.competing_evidence: Bitner+07 assigns K4.5 V±0.5 and 4470±140 K from a spectral-type scale with systematics; Harrison+16 IJHK synthetic spectrum gives 4750 K, subsolar Fe/C/Mg, and discusses apparent K3.5 versus inclination-corrected K2.5.
issues.why_it_matters: Roche distortion, inclination, irradiation/spots and metallicity affect spectral appearance; a donor Teff should not be interpreted as a unique single-star temperature.
issues.needed_action: For future online summaries, keep the calibrated subtype/temperature and IJHK atmosphere result as distinct method-tagged measurements; choose a canonical display only if a use case requires one.
